# readonly-type-mutation (MUT108)

Family: Mutation & State (MUT) · Heuristic · Opt-in · Severity `error` (a bug) · No automatic fix

Opt-in: changing in place a field that a standard type declares read-only (frozen dataclass / `NamedTuple` / `dataclass_transform` fields, `Final` / `ReadOnly` attributes, `ReadOnly` `TypedDict` keys), directly, through an alias, or in a helper.

!!! note "Heuristic"

    This rule is heuristic: a premise of its claim can be open ("What a report states" lists them), so a report can be wrong about the code. It runs only when `select` or `extend-select` names its code or name. It has not been measured yet. See [Rule Precision](../precision.md).

## What it does
Checks in-place changes of containers held in fields that a standard type declares read-only,
which type checkers let through because they only stop rebinding:

- a field that holds a container in a `@dataclass(frozen=True)`, a `NamedTuple`, or a class that a
  PEP 681 `dataclass_transform(frozen_default=True)` builds (a decorator function, base class, or
  metaclass carrying it, unless the class passes `frozen=False`), also on an instance of a
  subclass: `config.tags.append(...)`;
- an attribute declared `Final[...]` (`self.items: Final[list[int]] = []` in `__init__`, or a
  `Final` field of a dataclass or `NamedTuple`) or `ReadOnly[...]`, and a `ReadOnly` key of a
  `TypedDict` (`movie["names"].append(...)`).

A `Sequence` / `Mapping` / `AbstractSet` parameter handed to a helper that changes it is
`MUT110` (`readonly-param-mutation`), which shares this analysis.

Changes are followed through local aliases (`tags = config.tags; tags.append(...)`) and through
helpers, annotated or not and any number of calls deep, that change what they are handed: the
attribute itself (`add_default(config.tags)`) or the object holding it (`reset(config)`). Such a
change is reported at the call that hands the attribute or the object over, with the calls down
to the change as related locations. A helper that sees the object's type reports its own change
instead. A generator function changes what it is handed where its generator is iterated, and is
reported there; one that is created and never iterated changes nothing.

The rule does not report:

- rebinding or deleting the attribute (`config.tags = []`, `del config.tags`): type checkers
  report it;
- `object.__setattr__(...)`, `setattr(...)`, and `__dict__` writes: the deliberate way to set up a
  frozen instance, caches included;
- the class's own initialization: `__init__`, `__post_init__`, `__new__`, `model_post_init`,
  `__setstate__` changing their own instance, also through helpers that only run inside them;
- an instance the function constructs itself and fills before anyone else holds it
  (`index = Index({}, {}); index.names["a"] = 1`), directly or through a helper;
- fields declared `field(compare=False)` (state outside the instance's value, such as a cache);
  fields and attributes whose annotation is no container type (an object of a project class
  changes through its own methods); class variables (`ClassVar`); class-level constants of other
  classes; and module-level constants;
- a container inside the read-only one (`config.tables["a"].append(1)` with a frozen
  `tables: dict[str, list[int]]`): only the container in the read-only field counts.

Out of scope: `dataclass_transform`s defined outside the checked files, such as the frozen models
of `attrs` and Pydantic (heki does not analyze installed packages, so it cannot see the
transform); properties with a setter; `TypedDict` values read through `.get()`
(`movie.get("names")`); and objects whose class heki cannot see (an `Any` or unannotated
receiver).

## What a report states

A report states that the code changes in place a container held in a field that a standard type
declares read-only, directly, through an alias, or through the helpers shown.

Its premises:

- **Read-only field**: the class declares the field read-only (frozen dataclass, `NamedTuple`,
  `dataclass_transform`, `Final`, `ReadOnly`). Established from the declarations.
- **Instance**: the object is an instance of the class or of a subclass, by construction or
  annotation (assumption R2).
- **Changed in place**: an item store, a mutator method, or a helper changing its argument. Open
  through a helper: a change on one of its paths is enough.

## Why is this bad?
A frozen dataclass or a `NamedTuple` promises immutable instances, so code shares them freely: as
module-level defaults, in caches, or by handing the same value to several owners. An in-place
change of a container inside one is seen by every holder and changes the results of `==`. A
`Final` or `ReadOnly` declaration makes the same promise to the readers of the value. Type
checkers stop the rebinding, but not a change of the container inside, directly, through an
alias, or in a helper that receives a plain `list` or an unannotated value.

## Example
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


def add_default(tags):
    tags.append("default")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Config:
    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def configure(config: Config) -> None:
    add_default(config.tags)  # MUT108: changes the frozen `Config.tags` in place
```

Use instead:
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Config:
    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def configure(config: Config) -> Config:
    return replace(config, tags=(*config.tags, "default"))
```

## Fix safety
No automatic fix.

## Options
- `lint.extend-select = ["MUT108"]` (or `--extend-select MUT108`) enables the rule. It is
  opt-in: selecting the `MUT` prefix does not enable it.
- No other configuration: the rule reads standard `typing` and `dataclasses` declarations only.
